concepts.label: Hierarchical decomposition
concepts.lead: Examine a manageable part, then bring it back into the larger decision.
paragraphs: We divide a complex question into components that people can examine, then integrate what those components establish. A useful abstraction preserves the meanings, conditions, and evidence that affect how its result can be used.

Technical qualification, production capacity, and purchasing authority can be examined separately. A trial and a customer order may still need the same production line. Keeping that dependency visible lets us check the combined demands when the parts come together.

concepts.label: Convention based modeling
concepts.lead: Make deliberate choices about how a decision is described.
paragraphs: At Hermod Labs, decision patterns describe reusable overall approaches to decisions; workflows put them into practice. Reasoning patterns describe supporting methods, which configured apps apply. This is our organizing convention for connecting reusable structures to working reviews.

Shared meanings and explicit conditions let software automate declared consequences. Workflows can also contain calculations and review logic. People retain responsibility for goals, judgments, tradeoffs, choices, and authorizations.

concepts.label: Ontology engineering
concepts.lead: Preserve the distinctions a decision depends on.
paragraphs: An ontology defines the kinds of things a model recognizes and the relationships between them. Ontology engineering is the work of choosing, checking, and maintaining those meanings as our understanding changes.

A trial, its report, a technical finding, and permission to purchase play different roles. Keeping them distinct lets people follow the reasoning from evidence to action. A technical approval retains its scope when another team uses it.

shipmentExample.text: In Maya’s shipment review, the expense limit, available cash, and permission to spend are separate conditions. Having enough cash does not establish who may authorize the shipment. Keeping those meanings distinct helps the team review what the proposed movement actually requires.

concepts.label: Reasoning modules
concepts.lead: Work on one question without losing what its answer means.
paragraphs: A reasoning pattern describes a reusable method. A reasoning module brings methods, concepts, claims, rules, and conditions together around a scoped question. A configured app can make that assessment executable.

Technical qualification and purchasing authority can be separate modules within a supplier decision. Each preserves what it establishes, depends on, and leaves unresolved. Reusing an app carries those conditions forward.

concepts.label: Pattern languages
concepts.lead: Reuse an approach while keeping its context in view.
paragraphs: A pattern describes a reusable solution to a recurring problem, preserving its context, conditions, and rationale. A pattern language connects these solutions so people can combine and adapt them to the particulars of their work.

Our convention distinguishes decision patterns for the overall approach from reasoning patterns for supporting methods. Workflows put decision patterns into practice, using configured apps for reusable assessments alongside supporting calculations and review logic.

One decision pattern can use several reasoning patterns, and a reasoning pattern can serve several decision patterns. Different workflows and apps can implement variations. Shared meanings, compatible inputs, explicit conditions, and reviewed handoffs make those combinations dependable.

shipmentExample.text: Maya’s shipment review reuses a simple approach: check complete combinations against the requirements, then compare those that pass. Two apps use the same shipment facts and checks while applying different priorities: lowest expense or earliest arrival. The team can adapt that approach for another shipment without starting its reasoning from scratch.

concepts.label: Computational hermeneutics
concepts.lead: What may the next step rely on?
paragraphs: Reusing a reasoning method in another domain differs from relying on a particular finding. The method must fit the new question; the finding must establish what the next step needs. Preserve its subject, revision, status, scope, conditions and source when connecting it to another review.

“We can run the trial on Friday” may describe expected availability; it does not by itself reserve the line or authorize spending. People clarify the claim and examine its evidence and authority. Explicit models calculate the consequences of reviewed interpretations; they do not automatically establish equivalent meanings.

concepts.label: Requirements engineering
concepts.lead: State what an acceptable result must satisfy.
paragraphs: Requirements turn needs, constraints, and standards into conditions we can examine together. They give us a basis for checking whether a proposed combination of choices works and for seeing where a tradeoff arises.

A supplier change might require a qualifying trial, preserved customer deliveries, and spending authorization. A lower price may depend on a trial that cannot happen in time. Making those conditions explicit shows what would have to change.

concepts.label: Systems engineering
concepts.lead: Examine how the parts work together toward a purpose.
paragraphs: Systems engineering connects needs and requirements to how parts are designed, combined, tested, and used. It asks us to consider the interactions across people, equipment, procedures, and the wider operation.

A cheaper material could create more inspection work or slow production. We examine those consequences across the relevant boundaries and check whether the combined result serves the need that prompted the decision.

concepts.label: Feedback loops
concepts.lead: Connect what happens to the next decision.
paragraphs: We form a model, choose, act, observe, and compare the results with what we expected. Those observations can change an assumption, a method, or the requirements themselves. Keeping the original reasoning available makes that comparison possible.

If material passes its trial but slows regular production, the team can revisit the savings estimate. We ask what to observe, who will review it, and which findings should trigger reconsideration. We also examine loops within the work, such as rework creating pressure that produces more defects.

concepts.label: The arrangement problem
concepts.lead: Ask whether the whole combination can satisfy its requirements.
paragraphs: A plan describes what we intend to do. An arrangement represents the possible combinations of work, people, resources, permissions, and dependencies allowed by the rules and context. As work progresses and conditions change, the workable combinations can change too.

Three activities may each need three hours on a line with eight hours available. Every pair fits; all three do not. Checking the full arrangement reveals the shared constraint. Changes to availability can change which arrangements work. Any result remains bounded by the modeled choices and assumptions, with outstanding obligations kept visible.

shipmentExample.text: Maya’s direct and backup shipment options combine a ship point, timing, people, resources, and permissions. Both pass with a $6,500 expense limit. Lowering it to $5,000 rules out the $6,000 backup while leaving the $4,000 direct option available. Changing one condition changes the collection of workable combinations.

concepts.label: Assessment patterns
concepts.lead: An arrangement is a complete candidate combination. An assessment pattern defines what that candidate represents, how it is evaluated and what conclusion the evaluation can support.
paragraphs: An interpretation of evidence, an operating plan and an investigation with responses can share an arrangement foundation while answering different questions. Each needs its own admissibility conditions, assessment method and limits on what can be concluded.

Ontologies, phrase patterns, requirements and reasoning modules supply the foundations. Domain applications supply concrete meanings and records; workflows connect the resulting assessments to further questions and available responses. We design backward from the question people need answered.
